diff --git a/inflection/__init__.py b/inflection/__init__.py
index ffac5ce22e60816f18267d742455e4936b6d1c1a..dc49932f761a9abd9f8dd555078e9ad1a8352ee7 100644
--- a/inflection/__init__.py
+++ b/inflection/__init__.py
@@ -9,6 +9,7 @@
 
     :license: MIT, see LICENSE for more details.
 """
+import bisect
 import re
 import typing
 import unicodedata
@@ -371,12 +372,127 @@ def titleize(word: str) -> str:
       >>> titleize("raiders_of_the_lost_ark")
       'Raiders Of The Lost Ark'
 
+    If the string also contains lowercase letters, words of two or more
+    letters written entirely in capitals are taken to be acronyms and are
+    kept exactly as they are::
+
+      >>> titleize("NASA rocket launch")
+      'NASA Rocket Launch'
+      >>> titleize("read the HTTP spec")
+      'Read The HTTP Spec'
+
+    A string without any lowercase letters is titleized like any other::
+
+      >>> titleize("HELLO WORLD")
+      'Hello World'
+
     """
-    return re.sub(
+    title = re.sub(
         r"\b('?\w)",
         lambda match: match.group(1).capitalize(),
         humanize(underscore(word)).title()
     )
+    if any(char.islower() for char in word):
+        title = _restore_acronyms(title, word)
+    return title
+
+
+def _restore_acronyms(title: str, word: str) -> str:
+    """
+    Put the all-caps words of ``word`` back into ``title``, its titleized
+    form, spelled exactly as they are in ``word``.
+
+    Titleizing keeps the letters and digits of a string in their order; it
+    only changes their case and the separators between them, except that
+    :func:`humanize` drops a trailing ``_id``.  So the n-th letter or digit of
+    ``word`` becomes the n-th letter or digit of ``title``, which tells where
+    each acronym ended up.  The text found there is replaced only when it
+    holds the same letters and digits as the acronym.
+    """
+    word_positions = _alnum_skeleton(word)[1]
+    title_positions = _alnum_skeleton(title)[1]
+    pieces: typing.List[str] = []
+    copied = 0
+    for start, end in _acronym_spans(word):
+        first = bisect.bisect_left(word_positions, start)
+        last = bisect.bisect_left(word_positions, end)
+        if last > len(title_positions):
+            break  # dropped by humanize(), like the "ID" of "user_ID"
+        low = title_positions[first]
+        high = title_positions[last - 1] + 1
+        while high < len(title) and _is_mark(title[high]):
+            high += 1
+        acronym = word[start:end]
+        found = title[low:high]
+        if low >= copied and (
+            _alnum_skeleton(found)[0] == _alnum_skeleton(acronym)[0]
+        ):
+            pieces += [title[copied:low], acronym]
+            copied = high
+    pieces.append(title[copied:])
+    return ''.join(pieces)
+
+
+def _acronym_spans(text: str) -> typing.List[typing.Tuple[int, int]]:
+    """
+    Return the ``(start, end)`` slices of the all-caps words in ``text``.
+
+    A word is a run of letters and digits.  Runs without lowercase letters
+    that are joined by an apostrophe make up a single word, so ``DON'T`` is
+    one all-caps word, and the possessive ``NASA's`` contains the all-caps
+    word ``NASA``.  An all-caps word has at least two uppercase letters and
+    no lowercase ones.
+    """
+    spans: typing.List[typing.Tuple[int, int]] = []
+    for start, end in _word_spans(text):
+        if any(char.islower() for char in text[start:end]):
+            continue
+        if spans and spans[-1][1] == start - 1 and text[start - 1] == "'":
+            start = spans.pop()[0]
+        spans.append((start, end))
+    return [
+        (start, end) for start, end in spans
+        if sum(char.isupper() for char in text[start:end]) >= 2
+    ]
+
+
+def _word_spans(text: str) -> typing.Iterator[typing.Tuple[int, int]]:
+    """
+    Yield the ``(start, end)`` slice of every run of letters and digits in
+    ``text``.  A combining mark belongs to the run of the character it
+    decorates.
+    """
+    start: typing.Optional[int] = None
+    for index, char in enumerate(text):
+        if char.isalnum() or (start is not None and _is_mark(char)):
+            if start is None:
+                start = index
+        elif start is not None:
+            yield start, index
+            start = None
+    if start is not None:
+        yield start, len(text)
+
+
+def _alnum_skeleton(text: str) -> typing.Tuple[str, typing.List[int]]:
+    """
+    Return the case-folded letters and digits of ``text``, leaving out every
+    other character, along with the index in ``text`` that each of them comes
+    from.
+    """
+    letters: typing.List[str] = []
+    positions: typing.List[int] = []
+    for index, char in enumerate(text):
+        for folded in char.casefold():
+            if folded.isalnum():
+                letters.append(folded)
+                positions.append(index)
+    return ''.join(letters), positions
+
+
+def _is_mark(char: str) -> bool:
+    """Tell whether ``char`` is a combining mark, such as an accent."""
+    return unicodedata.category(char).startswith('M')
